text:
Anya: quick check — we need to pick a direction for internal APIs (REST edge vs gRPC end-to-end). main constraints: quota enforcement at gateway, tracing/telemetry continuity, and rollout UX for model/router changes. thoughts?
Matt: my +1 is proto-first gRPC inside the mesh, REST only at the external edge for browser/3p. less ambiguity on payloads and we get streaming. :thumbsup:
Lina: i'm worried about rollout UX. if we go proto-first, how do product/console teams see stable per-route metrics during canaries? dashboards expect consistent labels. question: does the gateway translate telemetry or do we push telemetry from services?
Sam: hybrid approach proposal: keep a thin REST edge that translates to gRPC and injects unified headers (tenant, quota-key, routed-model). services emit telemetry with those propagated labels. avoids changing existing console surface.
Jun: can we rely on translation layer to do quota accounting? i.e. gateway increments counters and enforces rate limits before translating. concern: double-counting when retries or multi-hop calls happen. need idempotent request-id semantics.
Anya: good point. also need to handle streaming/reranking where gateway can't fully understand proto — do we fallback to sampling for telemetry?
Matt: for sampling we should preserve trace IDs only, not attempt payload introspection. services should tag spans with model_id and route_policy. that keeps the console query path simple: trace->span tags.
Sam: we tried header set like this:
```
X-Tenant-ID: 12345
X-Quota-Key: tenant:12345:route:generate
X-Route-Policy: low-latency
X-Trace-Id: 01abcd
```
Gateway also emits a canonical route name (eg: "/api/v1/generate -> models/gpt-3.8q") which the console uses for aggregation.
Lina: the canonical route name is critical. without it the dashboards show both "/api/v1/generate" and "/v1/rpc.Generate" in panels. that confused pm demos last week. :grimacing:
Anya: what about error mapping? if the backend returns rich proto errors, the gateway should map them to well known REST codes for external clients but preserve proto.code for internal logs/alerts.
Jun: agree. proto error -> HTTP 500/429 mapping but keep internal error_code tag. also quotas should expose both "tokens" and "requests" buckets. some customers meter by tokens.
Matt: implementation note: avoid double-marshalling large responses. the gateway should pass through streaming byte chunks where possible for large generation streams. translation only for control plane requests.
Sam: that increases complexity for the gateway. path: implement a policy-based translator: for small RPCs do full proto->json, for streaming generations do transparent passthrough and just copy headers/traces. lightweight switch.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started: eng-runtime/model-router v2 -> 5% traffic (deploy id: dpl-2026-03-21-42)
Lina: can console show canary metrics split automatically by route and model variant? we should wire the rollout id to telemetry so panels can filter to the canary group.
Matt: yes — gateway should add header `X-Canary-ID` and services should tag spans. console saved views can then use `canary_id` filter.
Anya: security check — if gateway injects quota keys, we need HMAC or signed header to prevent users spoofing tenant/route. thought: sign with gateway key, verify in-service.
Sam: agreed. header format proposal: `X-GW-Signature: gw1|v1|<sig>` where sig = HMAC(key, tenant|route|ts). services verify with shared key via KMS rotation. lightweight and avoids adding auth calls.
Jun: audit log requirement: gateway must log every quota decision (allow/deny/overflow) to central event stream with route, tenant, tokens_used. that supports billing and disputes.
Anya: final question: rollout UX — do we lean on canaries at gateway (route split) or service-side feature flags? which gives easier rollback?
Lina: gateway-based split easier to reason about for ops and immediately visible in console. service-side flags are good for fine-grained feature gating but harder to observe globally. i'd pick gateway-first for model rollouts.
Matt: agree — gateway splits + service-side toggles for safety. implement telemetry hooks for both so console shows combined view.
deploy-bot: automated test run: integration-tests/gateway-translation passed (12/12) — artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/gateway-translation/2441234567/
Anya: next actions: 1) Sam to draft gateway translation RFC with header/hmac format and passthrough policy. 2) Jun to spec quota audit events + schema. 3) Lina to mock console panels for canary-id and canonical-route. please have drafts by EOD Friday.
Sam: on it. starting RFC now.
Jun: will sketch schema tonight.
Lina: mockups by Thursday morning.
Anya: thanks all — looks like consensus for hybrid REST-edge + proto-first internal gRPC with gateway-enforced quotas, signed headers, and telemetry tags for console. :tada:
